title: Gradient Accumulation and Micro-Batching
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of gradient accumulation and micro-batching in a PyTorch workflow.

content.intro: Gradient Accumulation and Micro-Batching: PyTorch tensors and models live on a device, and mixed precision changes how floating-point operations are represented. Hardware and operator support determine which settings are suitable. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Correct device placement avoids runtime mismatches, while carefully validated precision can reduce memory or time on supported hardware. For this lesson, focus on effective batch size and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
model = nn.Linear(2, 1)
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
optimizer.zero_grad()
for _ in range(2):
    loss = model(torch.ones(1, 2)).sum() / 2
    loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
print("two micro-batches accumulated")

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
